npcs.name: Thorgunna
npcs.idle: My Alf drowned in the swamp four winters ago. He came to my door last night.

npcs.name: Runemistress Gunnvor
npcs.idle: My brother went into the hagbui barrows for a sword. The hagbui keep what goes in.

quests.title: The Clay Child
quests.offer:
My son Alf drowned at the western ford four winters ago. Last night something knocked at my door and called me Mother. It looked like Alf. It was made of mud. Clay. It had his face.

I screamed and slammed the door. It went away crying. Will you [find out what it is]? I can't sleep. I can't stop hearing it cry.
quests.summary: Something made of clay, with her drowned son's face, knocked at Thorgunna's door and called her Mother.

steps.goal: Go to the western ford where Alf drowned
steps.text: Small footprints in the mud. Clay footprints - they dry and crumble as you watch. They lead west.

steps.goal: Cut through the forest vipers on the trail
Follow the trail to the clay jotuns' camp
steps.text: Clay jotuns, huge and slow, shaping figures from the swamp mud. Among the half-made giants, a small clay boy sits alone.

steps.say:
Are you from Mother? Did she send you?

The shaper made me out of the ford-mud. Where the boy fell in. He said the mud remembered the boy, so I do too. I remember Mother's soup. And her hands. I went to see her and she [screamed].

steps.text: The shaper slumps into a heap of wet clay. The little clay boy watches it with wide clay eyes.

stages.name: Leirr the Shaper
stages.announce: A clay jotun with long fingers rises from its work. 'That one is mine. I made it from a drowned thing. It is for the army.'

steps.goal: Bring the clay boy to Thorgunna
steps.say:
It's - he's - it's standing behind you. In the rain. And he's crumbling a little, at the edges.

It isn't Alf. I know that. But it remembers my soup. It remembers my hands.

If I [take him in], he'll fall apart at the next big rain - Ulf the seer says a month, maybe two. I'd have him a month. Or I [send him back] to the swamp, and the mud, and don't have to watch it happen again.

options.say: Come here. Come in. Mind the step. ...There. He's sitting by the fire. He's drying out. He says it's warm.
Go back. Go back to the ford. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I can't. ...He's going. He's not crying. That's worse.

kept.text: Take this. He made it for you, while he could.

sent.text: Take this. I can't look at it.

quests.title: The Unburied Thane
quests.offer:
This is GROUP work. The hagbui are draugr - barrow-dead - and their thane is old and terrible.

My brother Ketil went into the hagbui barrows in the north-west for our grandfather's sword, Leg-Biter, buried with the thane who killed him. Ketil didn't come out. Last week my seeing-stones showed him walking among the hagbui. Dead. Still walking.

Will you [go into the barrows]?
quests.summary: GROUP. Runemistress Gunnvor's brother went into the hagbui barrows for an ancestral sword and now walks among the draugr.

steps.goal: Go to the hagbui barrows in the north-west
steps.text: Barrow-mounds steaming in the cold. The dead walk between them, armed and patient.
Among them, one draugr wears a living man's ring - Gunnvor's family rune. Ketil, or what's left. He watches you and doesn't come closer.

clue.name: a runestone at the barrow mouth

steps.text: 'Here lies Ulfhedinn, who slew Gunnar Leg-Biter's-Bearer and took his sword into the dark. Who takes it out takes his place.' Ketil took it out. That's why he walks.
The thane falls, and the sword Leg-Biter clatters onto the barrow stones. Every hagbui on the mounds stops and turns towards it.

stages.name: Thane Ulfhedinn the Unburied
stages.announce: The barrow opens. Something huge and dead in rotten mail climbs out, an empty scabbard at its hip. 'WHO HOLDS MY SWORD?'

steps.say:
You've seen him. Ketil. And the sword.

The runes say whoever bears Leg-Biter out of the barrow takes the thane's place, so Ketil walks. If I [burn the barrows], the hagbui burn - all of them, Ketil too, his soul with them. They'll never walk again.

Or we [bury him with honour] - sword and all, in the thane's own barrow. He'll be the new thane. The hagbui will walk on. But he'll be Ketil, in a way. I can't. Tell me.

options.say: Then I'll carve the fire-runes myself. Tonight. ... Goodbye, Ketil. You always were the brave one.
Then he'll be thane. Thane of the barrows. Our grandfather would laugh. ...I'll visit him. Once a year. With mead he can't drink.

burned.text: Take something from my grandfather's hoard.

thane.text: Take something from my grandfather's hoard.
